# Bug Reports — unified-anoa-binary-terminal-cdp

> Note on the `[open]` markers below: `parseBugsFile()` in the jonggrang CLI
> recognises exactly two header states, `[open]` and `[task:<id>]`. There is no
> `[fixed]`, and a header it does not recognise is dropped from the parse
> entirely — so a resolved bug that has never been converted to a task has to
> stay `[open]` or vanish from `jonggrang bug list`. Resolution is therefore
> recorded in the body, starting with RESOLVED.
>
> Also note: `jonggrang bug --feature <id>` cannot file a bug non-interactively
> in this repo. The global option parser consumes `--feature` into
> WORK_FEATURE_ID before `cmdBug()` ever sees it, so with more than one feature
> present the command always exits with "Multiple features found. Use --feature
> <featureId>." Entries here are appended by hand in the format above.

## [open] bug-001 · 2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z
RESOLVED in phase 14 (parser extracted to src/terminal/frame_bytes.cpp, guard fixed, regression tests TERM-BYTES-02/03 in tests/unit/test_frame_bytes.cpp, integration case THTTP-09 in tests/integration/terminal_http.test.js). Original report: src/terminal/render_http_client.cpp parsePpm(): unsigned underflow in the pixel-length guard permits an unbounded out-of-bounds read. After readInt(maxval) consumes the last byte of the body, `++pos` (the "single whitespace byte after maxval" step) leaves pos == data.size()+1. The guard `data.size() - pos < need` is size_t arithmetic, so it wraps to SIZE_MAX and always passes; `QByteArray(data.data() + pos, need)` then copies w*h*3 bytes from past the end of the string. w and h are read off the wire, so a truncated or hostile response of exactly "P6 4000 4000 255" from the --term-host/--term-port endpoint reads ~48 MB out of bounds and will typically segfault. Verified with a standalone repro of the guard (/tmp/ppm_probe.cpp): for "P6 1 1 255", size=10 pos=11 and size-pos evaluates to 18446744073709551615. Inherited unchanged from tools/anoa-term/anoa_term.cpp, but the function was rewritten into the new file on this branch. Fix: test `pos > data.size() || data.size() - pos < need` before the copy. — As applied: the guard is `pos > len || (unsigned long long)(len - pos) < need`, `need` is computed in 64-bit so a wire-chosen w*h*3 cannot overflow the comparison, and readInt() now refuses a dimension past 10^8 rather than overflowing an int on the way in. Confirmed red first: TERM-BYTES-02 failed and TERM-BYTES-03 took SIGSEGV against the pre-fix parser.

## [open] bug-002 · 2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z
RESOLVED in phase 14 (regression tests TERM-INPUT-01/03 in tests/unit/test_terminal_ui.cpp). Original report: src/terminal/terminal_ui.cpp processInput(): a CSI escape sequence split across two stdin reads is discarded rather than buffered, contradicting the contract documented at terminal_ui.h:91 ("a partial escape sequence is buffered until the rest turns up"). When the buffer ends with exactly the two bytes ESC '[', the guard at line 541 (`i + 1 >= buf.size()`) does not fire, the arrow-key test at line 550 and the SGR-mouse test at line 560 both need `i + 2 < buf.size()` and are skipped, so control falls to `i += 2` at line 618 and buf.erase(0, i) drops the prefix. The remainder then arrives on the next read as a bare final byte: an up-arrow split this way types the literal character "A" into the page instead of moving the caret, and a split mouse report leaks "<0;12;7M" as typed text. Only the two-byte-tail case is affected; longer partial sequences are correctly retained. Fix: after confirming buf[i+1] == '[', break out of the loop when the sequence is not yet complete, the same way the SGR branch already does at line 583. — As applied: `if (i + 2 >= buf.size()) break;` immediately after the `buf[i + 1] == '['` check, which also made the now-redundant `i + 2 < buf.size()` conditions on the arrow and SGR branches unnecessary; both were dropped so the guard lives in one place. Confirmed red first: both regression tests failed against the pre-fix parser, and the captured status bar showed the leaked `typed "<`.

## [open] bug-004 · 2026-08-01T15:45:00.000Z
src/http/http_server.cpp: /render/screenshot.ppm truncates any response over roughly 1 MB while Content-Length still declares the full size, so the endpoint reports success and delivers a short body. Measured against a 1280x720 page: `?w=320&h=240` declares 172815 bytes and delivers all of them; `?w=800&h=600` declares 1080015 and delivers 0 to an HTTP client; the unscaled frame declares 2764816 and delivers 0, with a raw socket receiving ~327 KB before the peer closes. /render/screenshot.png is unaffected (19 KB, intact), which points at response size rather than at the capture. Reproduces identically with --headless and headed, and on code untouched by the terminal work — the write path is `socket->write(response); socket->flush(); socket->disconnectFromHost();`, which does not wait for the write buffer to drain before closing, so anything past the first socket buffer is discarded. Not found by any existing suite because every caller in the repo asks for a scaled frame: the terminal viewer sizes its request to the cell grid, which is far below the threshold. A client fetching a full-resolution PPM — the documented way to get one — gets a silently truncated image. Fix: wait for bytesWritten/waitForBytesWritten before disconnecting, or disconnect from a bytesWritten handler once the buffer is empty. Found while verifying that the new headed window chrome had not changed what /render/* captures; it had not.

## [open] bug-003 · 2026-08-01T05:20:00.000Z
src/terminal/render_http_client.cpp httpRequest(): the socket has no SO_RCVTIMEO, no SO_SNDTIMEO and no bound on connect(), so a peer that accepts the connection and then sends nothing wedges the entire viewer. This was survivable when the frame loop was a blocking select(); since it became a QTimer callback (commit eb3e2c1) the blocking read() runs *on the Qt event loop*, and everything that would let a user out depends on that loop still turning: the QSocketNotifier on stdin never fires again, so Ctrl-C is never read; ISIG is off in raw mode, so byte 3 is not a signal either; and SIGTERM is handled by onSignalQuit(), which only sets a flag that the never-reached frame tick polls. The process therefore survives Ctrl-C, SIGINT and SIGTERM alike and needs SIGKILL, leaving the terminal in raw mode on the alt screen (the atexit(restoreTerminal) hook does not run on SIGKILL). Reproduced by THTTP-08 in tests/integration/terminal_http.test.js, which answers the 8x8 pre-flight probe and then stalls every frame request; it is committed as `it.fails()` and passes today *because* the wedge happens, so it turns red the moment a timeout lands. Also filed as code-quality finding #3 in phase 12, where the cost was lower. Fix: set SO_RCVTIMEO/SO_SNDTIMEO on the socket after socket(), bound connect() (non-blocking connect plus select, or SO_SNDTIMEO where it applies), and report the expiry through frameFailed() so the status bar says "timed out" rather than freezing on the last frame.
